out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Shellstock Label Marked, Last Date Served/Sold Info
violations.observation: The date when the last shellstock (fresh mussels and clams) from the container is sold or served is not recorded on the tag or label.
violations.corrective_action: The identity of the source of shellstock (oysters, clams, mussels) that are sold or served shall be maintained by retaining shellstock tags or labels and marking the tag or label with the date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served. CDI: CFM recorded date of last sale for previously sold fresh clams and mussels. EHS instructed CFM to record last date of sale for fresh shellstaock (mussels and clams).

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: open/ wrapped deli sliced cheeses (provolone, cheddar, pepper jack) and deli meats (turkey, ham, pastrami, etc.) stored inside the Thermokool walk in refrigerator (main kitchen).
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. CDI: CFM datemarked open/ wrapped deli sliced cheeses (provolone, cheddar, pepper jack) and deli meats (turkey, ham, pastrami, etc.) stored inside the Thermokool walk in refrigerator (main kitchen) with remaining hold date before discard ( 6 remaining days).

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Two unlabeled working chemical spray bottles of poisonous and toxic materials (degreaser) are not properly labeled with a common name.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. CDI: CFM labeled the two chemical spray bottle with common name (degreaser).

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: recently sliced tomatoes (47F), coleslaw (49F), and pineapple salsa (47F) cooling inside the top part of the Beverage Air 2 Dr/ 2 DWR preptop refrigerator on main kitchen prepline.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI: CFM relocated sliced tomatoes, coleslaw,and coleslaw to blast chiller to rapidly cool to 41F before relocating back to cold hold units on prepline.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: Observed raw diced tuna improperly thawing in uncut ROP vacuum packaging inside Beverage Air 2 DWR/ 2 Dr preptop refrigerator on the prepline in the pantry kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: CDI: CFM cut ROP vacuum packaging to allow raw diced tuna properly to properly thaw.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: multiple squeeze bottles (oil, water, sauces) and containers of seasonings and spices (salt, etc.) throughout the prep area.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS instructed CFM to label food items no longer in the original container and not easily identifiable with common food name. CFM called onsite engineer/ maintenance personnel to repair both Avantico 2 Dr UC refrigerator in the expo area.

violations.observation: Observed frozen tuna steaks improperly thawing in uncut vacuum packaging in food prep counter in kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: CDI: CFM cut frozen tuna steaks vacuum packaging and thawed under refrigeration.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils Self-Draining Position/Covered/Inverted
violations.observation: Observed several ice bins that have been cleaned stored directly on floor and not inverted/ covered throughout the kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Clean equipment and utensils shall be stored covered or inverted to prevent contamination. CDI: CFM stored ice bins on shelf inverted near the ice machine in kitchen area.

out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Parasite Destruction
violations.observation: The following fish offered for service or sale in the ready-to-eat form was not frozen to ensure parasite destruction: fresh tuna and salmon served cooked to order.
violations.corrective_action: Before service or sale in ready-to-eat form, raw or partially cooked fish shall be: 1) frozen and stored at a temperature of -4F or below for a minimum of 7 days in a freezer, or 2) frozen at -31F or below until solid and stored at -31F or below for a minimum of 15 hours, or 3) frozen at -31F or below until solid and stored at -4F or below for a minimum of 24 hours. EHS instructed CFM to provide parasite destruction letter for the fresh tuna and salmon from the supplier.

violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Observed debris on the interior the ice machine in the upstairs kitchen and is not being cleaned as required.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. CDI: CFM cleaned the interior of the ice machine.

violations.title: Mechanical Warewashing, Sanitization Pressure
violations.observation: The pressure gauge for the high temperature ware washing machine located in the downstairs kitchen was observed below 5 PSI or 30 PSI. Observed pressure was between 30- 35 PSI at time of inspection. water temperature in the manifold servicing the high temperature warewashing machine was below the minimum allowable level of 165F for a stationary rack single temperature machine. The thermostat read @TEMPERATURE@.
violations.corrective_action: The flow pressure of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse in a warewashing machine shall be within the range specified on the machine manufacturer's data plate and may not be less than 5 PSI or more than 30 PSI as measured in the water line immediately downstream or upstream from the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse control valve. EHS instructed CFM to service dish machine for high temperature ware washing machine’s pressure to ensure it is between 5 and 30 PSI.

out_items.name: Compliance with variance, specialized process, HACCP

violations.title: ROP, HACCP Plan in Place
violations.observation: The establishment does not have an approved HACCP plan for the food that is packaged using the Reduced Oxygen Packaging (ROP) process to vacuum packaging NY strip steaks onsite, freezing in walk in freezer, thawing, and using for more than 48 hours.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment that packages a time/temperature control for safe food using a Reduced Oxygen Packaging method shall have a HACCP plan that contains the information specified under 8-201.14(D) and that: 1) identifies the food to be packaged, 2) requires that the packaged food shall be maintained at 41F or less, has a water activity of 0.91 or less, a pH of 4.6 or less, is a meat or poultry product that is cured at a food processing plant, is received in an intact package, or is a food with a high level of competing organisms, 3) describes how the package shall be prominently and conspicuosly labeled on the principal display panel in bold type on a contrasting background with instructions to maintain the food at 41F or below and discard the food if within 14 calendar days of its packaging, 40 limits the refrigerated shelf life to no more than 14 calendar days from packaging to consumption or the origjnal manufacturer's 'sell by' or 'use by' date whichever occurs first, 5) includes operational procedures that prohibit contacting food with bare hands, identifies a designated work area and the method by which physical barriers or methods of separation minimizes cross contamination, access to the processing equipment is limited to responsible trained personnel, and cleaning and sanitizing procedures for equipment/utensils is monitored, and 6) describes the training program that ensures that the individual responsible for the ROP operation understands the concepts required for a safe operation, understands the equipment and facilites, and procedures specified in this section. CDI: EHS instructed CFF to discontinue ROP food items until they are approved through the health department. EHS provided CFM with ROP and HACCP application process info. WESTWOOD COUNTRY CLUB (Inspection Date: 08/28/2025) Page 3 of 4

out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Wash Temp for Hot Water Warewashing Machines
violations.observation: The wash water temperature of the hot water sanitizing warewashing machine is not meeting the manufacturer's specifications. The minimum temperature required TEMPERATURE is 150 while the actual temperature was observed was 123F.
violations.corrective_action: The temperature of the wash solution in spray type warewashers that use hot water to sanitize may not be less than: 1) 165F for a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 2) 150F for a stationary rack, dual temperature machine, 3) 160F for a single tank, conveyor, dual temperature machine, or 4) 150F for a multitank, conveyor, multitemperature machine.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Plumbing connections under the 3-compartment sinks piping are leaking.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.
